title: Boktai: The Sun Is in Your Hand
subtitle: The cartridge asks for sunlight
summary: Boktai: The Sun Is in Your Hand is Konami's Game Boy Advance action role-playing adventure about Django, a young vampire hunter carrying the Gun Del Sol. A light sensor built into the cartridge measures real sunlight and connects the player's surroundings with the energy available inside the game. Produced by Hideo Kojima, the adventure makes that physical relationship part of its identity rather than an optional accessory. Hunting the undead requires attention to the world beyond the screen, because the light falling on the handheld can affect the tools available to its hero.
body: Boktai: The Sun Is in Your Hand is Konami's Game Boy Advance action role-playing adventure about Django, a young vampire hunter carrying the Gun Del Sol. A light sensor built into the cartridge measures real sunlight and connects the player's surroundings with the energy available inside the game. Produced by Hideo Kojima, the adventure makes that physical relationship part of its identity rather than an optional accessory. Hunting the undead requires attention to the world beyond the screen, because the light falling on the handheld can affect the tools available to its hero.

The Gun Del Sol stores the energy gathered through the sensor, allowing Django to spend that reserve during an encounter. When it is exhausted and no sunlight is available, avoiding enemies becomes important until a Solar Station can provide another charge. The physical resource therefore changes the immediate choices inside the adventure. A player carrying a well-prepared weapon can confront a threat directly, while the same route may call for caution when the reserve is low. The sensor affects how the hunter approaches a situation rather than simply changing a decorative meter.

Setting the local time and time zone lets the game estimate sunrise and sunset, connecting its fictional day with the player's location. The surroundings respond through details such as morning birds and an orange glow toward evening. Sunlight can also help restore a Solar Tree damaged by the darkness surrounding the Immortals. These effects extend the cartridge's central idea beyond firing the gun. The light outside becomes part of both the hunter's practical resources and the condition of a world whose changing atmosphere follows the passage of the real day.
story_headings: The gun can run out of daylight
The time of day reaches the landscape
